grade.first_issue: Rule E applies at the inductive step: the induction hypothesis concerns V-sets arising from a sequence satisfying the original greedy rule, but W_{n,p} comes merely from a subcollection of the supports S_i. No sequence satisfying that rule, with an initial term having at most k-1 prime factors, is constructed. Thus the asserted stabilization of W_{n,p}, and hence of V_n, is unsupported.
grade.summary: The hitting-set formulation and the argument that stabilization of V_n would yield translational periodicity are meaningful and largely correct. However, stabilization is the central structural claim, and the proposed induction does not prove it. Repairing this requires a new finiteness/structure argument comparable to the main content of the reference solution, so the proof is capped at 3 by Rule E.
strengths: Correctly reformulates each finite-stage admissibility set V_n using hitting sets and finite unions of sets of multiples.
Conditional on eventual stabilization, the periodicity of V_N and the resulting index shift are essentially correct.
The idea of extending the enumeration backward can be justified using V_N subseteq V_i and the greedy minimality of each a_{i+1}.

errors.description: The induction hypothesis is inapplicable to W_{n,p}. Having a hitting set S_1\setminus\{p\} of size k-1 does not make the relevant subcollection arise from another greedy sequence. Indeed, for arbitrary constraints, even a common one-prime hitting set does not imply stabilization: sets {q,r_i} all have the hitting set {q}, while their finite-stage admissibility sets continue shrinking.

The assertion that every inclusion-minimal hitting set has size at most |S_1| merely because S_1 is a hitting set is false. For example, for edges {p,q}, {p,r}, {p,s}, the set {q,r,s} is an inclusion-minimal hitting set of size 3 although the first edge has size 2. This assertion is not subsequently essential.

The backward-extension paragraph states V_N=V_{N-1}, which does not follow from stabilization stated only for n>=N unless N is first increased. The backward induction also omits the actual argument using V_N subseteq V_i; this part is routinely repairable once stabilization is available.
